top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is induced proximity, a general physical-chemical principle in which a small molecule acts as an adaptor whose ternary-complex cooperativity and residence time set degradation rates. The mechanism is reproduced by many groups with structures and kinetics, so it is secure at the molecular level even before an approved degrader. Crews and Deshaies conceived the PROTAC concept and Handa's cereblon work gives the glue strand its mechanism, so the three names cover both strands under one citation. The cost, accepted openly, is that Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito are omitted. C-N coupling (P002) is next because attribution and maturity are the cleanest, though I still doubt it opens much beyond the 2010 prize. Sequencing (P003) follows because of contested platform credit and the chemistry-versus-technology boundary. No award ranks last since several mature, well-attributed achievements are available.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I am a Lund colleague of Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai and my field overlaps with Daniel Aili, but I have no tie to any named laureate in P001, P002 or P003
